newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOCOM PGM prices surge on tight near-term supplies.
newsitem.headline: TOCOM PGM prices surge on tight near-term supplies.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo platinum group metals futures ended sharply higher on Monday, led by a surge in nearby months, reflecting tight near-term supplies caused by the Russian suspension of sales, traders said.

Animated short-covering by private investors, especially in nearby contracts boosted futures prices while trade in the physical market was virtually brought to a halt because of the extreme tightness in supplies, they said.
Spot June platinum, which has no daily limit, rocketed by 143 yen to end at 1,803 yen, while limitless June palladium surged by 111 yen per gram to close at a record high 879 yen.

In platinum, July, August, October and December rose by their 50 yen per gram limit, with benchmark April ending up 12 at 1,396 yen. July and August palladium rose by their 24 yen per gram limit, and benchmark April ended up 17 yen at 582 yen.
Traders expected nearby PGM prices to continue rising.

"A lack of liquidity in the spot market and surging short-term lease rates made arbitrage trade impossible. Until Russian supplies start flowing into the market, the crazy market will continue," one trader said.
Gold futures ended lower, not helped by strength in PGMs, as the yen's firmness against the dollar pressured the market.
Gold futures ranged from 19 yen to 29 yen per gram lower. Benchmark April gold ended off 27 yen at 1,244 yen.
Gold prices opened lower, but further losses were limited partly due to bargain-hunting.
Spot gold was quoted at $343.70/344.00 at 0755 GMT, against $343.20/70 in New York on Friday.
"A surge in PGM prices is likely to provide spot gold prices support, but a sharp rise is unlikely," one trader said.
Japan-Russia PGM supply talks for 1997 will continue until June 11. Benchmark silver ended 3.3 yen per 10 grams down at 176.1 yen.
